name: simulation
fault_schedule: The committed JSON fixture supplies fixed identities, input, logical time, failure timeout, and exact expected trace. The first two owner responses are lost, node B crashes, logical time advances to eviction, then the same request retries through the stable endpoint.
assertions: Production routing, topology, membership and replay decisions execute under the fixed schedule.
The acknowledged mutation and original result survive response loss, owner crash and ownership movement without a second application.
Forwarding preserves operation identity, input digest, deadline, method and bounded hop metadata; typed failures are preserved.
Changed input is rejected by durable replay, the modeled stale-admission boundary rejects the withdrawn node, and the operation makes bounded progress after movement.
Independent negative controls reject missing atomic outcomes and stale-owner acknowledgement.
limitations: In-memory conditional S3, transactional durability, node lifecycle and admission models; production Manager fencing, native SlateDB and real S3 remain separate fault gates.
The fixed first proof has no random choices; seed zero records that fact. Workload generation and schedule minimization remain future coverage.
